correctness.rationale: PASS: on q^9 Hermitian 3×3 matrices over F_{q²}, the trace pairing diagonalizes the translation-invariant rank distance. Count totally isotropic 1- and 2-spaces for each dual rank s=0..3, recover P1(s),P2(s),P3(s), and verify each nonprincipal row sums to -1. The s=1,2 powered multipliers remain strictly negative because their rank-three coefficients dominate rank-two growth, while s=3 has unique increasing root Φ_q(p)=q³3^p−q(q²−q+1)2^p−q²+q−1. At Φ=0 only dual rank-three is flat, multiplicity q³(q−1)²(q²+1)(q²+q+1). Schoenberg Gram yields dimension q^9−1 below threshold, q^9−1−multiplicity at boundary. The derivative Φ′(0)=q³log(3/2)+(q²−q)log2 gives q³β→1/log(3/2). Independently checked all spectral sign classes and roots q=2,3,4,5,7,11 (q=2 β=0.187962707562, dimension 231). Full checker source reviewed, including actual F4/F9 constructions; finite checks support rather than prove all q.

originality.rationale: PASS best of knowledge: the primary Gow–Lavrauw–Sheekey–Vanhove Hermitian rank-distance study develops association-scheme characters and constant-rank-distance code bounds but not exact powered negative type or 3×3 endpoint Hilbert rank. Cioabă–Gupta (2021/2022) full arXiv paper explicitly gives Hermitian forms graph eigenmatrices and solves single-distance-graph eigenvalue ordering conjectures; it does not state the exponent-dependent weighted combination, threshold or endpoint rank. Resultary searches for identical Hermitian formulas and broader families found no earlier same result, though previously known Fourier eigenmatrices can make priority subtle. No claim to novelty of classical eigenmatrices.
residual_risks: The Hermitian eigenmatrix is classical; a historical theorem on squared Euclidean embeddings or general weighted association-scheme radial kernels may imply this cutoff without naming negative type.
Cioabă–Gupta explicitly includes d=3 small eigenmatrix cases; all individual eigenvalues are known and not credited as new.
